data.name: Huckleberry Falls
data.detailed_description:
The township of Huckleberry has fallen into chaos! Undead roam freely and a sinister cult seek to bring on the end of the world.

A match puzzle game with RPG elements. Set in a post apocalyptic world where survivors must band together.

Use a full arsenal of weapons and explosives as you journey to put an end to the fall of Huckleberry.





  • A new match 3 mechanic that combines Tetris like shapes with Bomberman blasts
  • Charge up your amulets of power to unleash devastating spells
  • 100+ handcrafted levels of zombie blasting fun
  • Master 8 game modes as you journey to find the origin of the outbreak
  • Battle fearsome bosses for big rewards
  • Rescue survivors each with unique talents that can be tailored to your play style
  • Compete against your friends and earn your way onto the leader boards

reviews.review:
Huckleberry Falls takes the familiar foundation of a matching puzzle game and pushes it in a considerably stranger direction, surrounding its colorful board mechanics with zombies, survivors, explosives, magic, and a post-apocalyptic storyline. Developed and published by Fatcat Games, it is designed as a free-to-play puzzle experience with light RPG elements rather than a conventional match-three title. Its unusual mixture of casual puzzle mechanics and an undead apocalypse gives it a personality that immediately separates it from more traditional games in the genre.

The central puzzle system revolves around arranging and matching pieces while taking advantage of their shapes and positions. There is more emphasis on spatial planning than simply finding three identical objects sitting next to one another. Explosives add another layer to the board, allowing carefully arranged moves to produce satisfying chain reactions. Learning how pieces interact and figuring out where an explosion will have the greatest effect makes successful turns feel deliberate rather than purely dependent on spotting obvious matches. The system remains approachable enough for casual play, but efficient solutions reward players who think ahead.

Combat-inspired mechanics provide much of the game's personality. Bombs and other weapons fit naturally into the zombie setting, while magical abilities offer another way to manipulate difficult situations. Amulets can be charged and used to activate powerful spells, creating moments where accumulated resources can completely change the outcome of a troublesome encounter. These special abilities also help break up the standard matching routine. Instead of every stage being solved through exactly the same sequence of actions, players gradually gain additional options for controlling the board and dealing with threats.

Progression incorporates some light RPG concepts without turning the game into a complicated role-playing experience. Survivors can be rescued throughout the adventure, and their different talents contribute to the player's growing collection of useful abilities. This gives the campaign a stronger sense of advancement because completing stages is not solely about increasing a score. Building up a capable group of survivors, unlocking useful options, and becoming better equipped against increasingly dangerous opposition provides a reason to continue beyond the immediate satisfaction of finishing another puzzle.

The campaign is surprisingly substantial for a relatively modest puzzle game. More than 100 handcrafted levels are paired with eight game modes, while boss encounters periodically provide a change of pace and opportunities for greater rewards. The variety does not completely eliminate the repetition inherent to a matching puzzle game, but it helps prevent the experience from becoming one endless sequence of identical boards. A larger mystery involving the origins of the outbreak also ties the levels together and provides a straightforward narrative motivation for progressing through Huckleberry's ruined world.

Its presentation is memorable mainly because of the contrast between accessible puzzle gameplay and the darker subject matter surrounding it. Zombies and an apocalyptic cult would normally suggest an action or horror game, yet here they become the backdrop for matching pieces, charging spells, and setting off elaborate explosions. The combination is intentionally unconventional and gives the game a certain charm despite its comparatively simple visuals. Players expecting modern production values or an elaborate cinematic story will find something much smaller in scope, but the straightforward presentation keeps attention focused on the puzzle board.

There is a respectable collection of supporting features as well. The game is primarily a single-player experience and includes Steam achievements, Trading Cards, Steam Cloud functionality, and leaderboards. Leaderboards are particularly appropriate because the puzzle mechanics naturally encourage more efficient play and stronger scores. Hardware requirements are also very modest, making it an easy game to run on older or lower-powered Windows computers.

Steam Deck compatibility is a notable advantage. The game is officially Steam Deck Verified, with its core functionality working through the handheld's controls and its interface remaining usable on the smaller display. Controller prompts and general navigation are appropriately supported, while the game can run using settings suitable for the device. Its viewpoint and methodical pacing also translate naturally to portable play, although demanding visual settings can still make sensible performance adjustments worthwhile for players prioritizing battery life or consistent performance.

Huckleberry Falls is ultimately at its best when treated as an experimental puzzle hybrid. Its matching system is easy to understand, while bombs, spells, survivor abilities, bosses, multiple modes, and RPG-style progression give the formula additional depth. It cannot entirely escape repetition, and players looking for a deep RPG or sophisticated zombie adventure may find its systems comparatively lightweight. For puzzle fans, however, the unusual combination of mechanics creates something distinctive enough to deserve attention.

The game succeeds by taking a familiar genre and giving it an eccentric identity rather than attempting to reinvent puzzle gaming completely. Its sizable collection of handcrafted stages provides plenty to work through, while progression and special abilities create enough incentive to continue experimenting with the board. As a free-to-play experience, it offers a surprisingly broad package and should appeal most strongly to players who enjoy casual puzzle games but want additional strategy and progression surrounding the basic matching formula.

Rating: 7/10
